Introduction

Apeace (formerly known as Double B 21 and A-Peace) was a South Korean boy group known for its unusually large lineup and long-term focus on the Japanese entertainment market. Originally debuting in 2010 with 21 members, the group was divided into smaller sub-units such as Sky, Earth, River, and Burning. They rebranded to Apeace by the end of 2010 and launched their full-scale Japanese activities in 2011 with a three-team structure: Lapis, Jade, and Onyx. Each originally composed of seven members, the units were later rebranded as Lapis5, Jade5, and Onyx5, and promoted with five members in each.

Apeace was often referred to as the “Korean male AKB48” due to their daily live performances and fan-centric model. They performed over 2,000 times at their dedicated K Theater in Ebisu, Tokyo, drawing hundreds of thousands of fans over several years. Their Japanese debut mini-album, We Are the One, was released in 2011 and featured tracks like “Lover Boy,” while their self-titled full album followed in 2012. Despite being a K-pop group, most of their discography was in Japanese, with occasional Korean-language releases later in their career.

The group underwent several lineup changes over the years, adopting a graduation system until 2014 that allowed members to leave and be replaced. By the time of their disbandment, the group had decreased to 12 active members, with others on hiatus or serving in the military. Their final years saw them exploring Korean releases again, such as “Feel So Good” in 2019 and “Gentleman - Party All Night -” in 2020.

Apeace officially disbanded on December 31, 2021, as announced by their Japanese agency earlier that year.
